f: A multi-day cloudburst plus a glacial-lake overflow at Chorabari sent a wall of water through Kedarnath valley.
Death toll ~5,700 presumed dead; one of India's worst natural disasters.
Kedarnath town and pilgrim routes were largely destroyed; the temple itself survived.
Over 100,000 pilgrims and residents stranded; days-long military airlift followed.
Triggered by a M9.1 megathrust quake off Sumatra; waves crossed the Bay of Bengal in hours.
India recorded ~10,700 deaths; Tamil Nadu was worst hit.
Nagapattinam district alone lost ~6,000 people — mostly fishing communities.
Led to India's national tsunami early-warning system (INCOIS, 2007).
Worst flooding in Kerala in ~a century, driven by extreme monsoon rainfall.
~483 deaths; over 1 million people moved to relief camps.
35 of 54 dams were opened — the first time in decades for some, incl. Idukki.
Damage estimated near ₹40,000 crore (~$5.7B).
M7.7 intraplate quake on Republic Day; felt across western India and Pakistan.
~20,000 killed, ~167,000 injured; Bhuj, Anjar and Bhachau devastated.
Around 400,000 homes destroyed; ~$5–7B in damage.
Drove India's modern seismic building codes and the Gujarat rebuild program.
First super cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal since 1999 (satellite: 17→18 May intensification).
~128 deaths across India & Bangladesh; Kolkata and the Sundarbans hammered.
Costliest cyclone in North Indian Ocean history — ~$13 billion damage.
~3 million evacuated ahead of landfall despite the COVID lockdown.
Strongest cyclone to strike Odisha since the 1999 super cyclone.
~89 deaths — kept low by a landmark 1.2 million-person evacuation.
Puri & Bhubaneswar saw widespread power and telecom collapse.
UN praised Odisha's 'near-zero-casualty' preparedness model.
~40 tonnes of methyl isocyanate gas leaked from the Union Carbide plant.
~3,800 died within days; estimates of 15,000+ deaths over time.
Widely called the world's worst industrial disaster.
Site contamination and health effects persist across generations.
A rock-and-ice avalanche off Ronti Peak triggered a sudden flash flood.
Surged down the Rishiganga & Dhauliganga rivers; ~200 dead or missing.
Destroyed the Rishiganga plant and flooded the Tapovan-Vishnugad hydro tunnel.
Highlighted rising glacial-hazard risk in the fragile Himalaya.
Progressive ground sinking cracked homes across the Himalayan pilgrimage town.
Over 860 buildings developed fissures; hundreds of families evacuated.
Linked to construction load, drainage and nearby tunnelling on unstable slopes.
A live warning on unchecked development in the young Himalaya.
Heaviest rainfall in Chennai in ~100 years, worsened by a strong El Niño.
~290+ deaths across Tamil Nadu; the airport shut for days.
Unregulated wetland loss on the Adyar/Cooum floodplain intensified damage.
Economic losses estimated at $3 billion+.
Struck near Paradip at Category-5 strength — India's most intense recorded cyclone.
A 5–6 m storm surge pushed ~20 km inland; ~9,900 killed.
~1.67 million homes damaged; Jagatsinghpur (Ersama) worst hit.
Catalysed India's modern cyclone-shelter and preparedness program.
M7.6 quake with epicentre near Muzaffarabad, on the India–Pakistan divide.
On the Indian (J&K) side ~1,400 died — Uri, Tangdhar and Baramulla worst hit.
Total regional toll exceeded 86,000, mostly in Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
Triggered large cross-border relief and temporary LoC crossings.
A glacial-lake outburst from South Lhonak Lake surged down the Teesta river.
The flood destroyed the 1,200 MW Teesta-III dam at Chungthang.
~100 killed or missing; towns downstream to Rangpo were inundated.
Climate-driven lake growth had made South Lhonak a known standing hazard.
944 mm of rain in 24 h at Santacruz — a record single-day deluge.
~1,094 deaths in Maharashtra; the city was paralysed for days.
The choked, encroached Mithi River sharply worsened the flooding.
Prompted the BRIMSTOWAD storm-water and Mithi remediation programs.
